subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC qualification — connectivity & acceptance questions
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Trent <sam.trent@cedarcare.com>, Dr. Priya Rao <priya@cedarcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC qualification — connectivity & acceptance questions

Thanks for taking the time this morning. Quick recap + asks to keep momentum moving toward a pilot: 

Summary of what we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary driver: CedarCare needs PHI-processing inference for clinical triage; client must demonstrate strict data residency and limited egress.
- Desired deployment: Private VPC in customer account for prod, with an option for air-gapped on-prem for long-term regulated workloads.
- Acceptance bar: no outbound internet from production nodes; audit logs with 1-year retention; KMS/HSM integration for key control; SOC2 artifacts for vendor review.

Technical constraints you called out
- Prod hosts cannot initiate outbound connections to public endpoints (only controlled peering or private endpoints).
- Ingress will be via an internal load balancer; plan for MTU and path MTU discovery checks.
- Expected concurrent inference: ~120 concurrent requests, 10–15 RPS average, peak bursts up to 60 RPS.

Concrete next steps (owner / ETA)
1) CedarCare to share a network diagram showing current VPC boundaries, NAT/egress controls, and any transit gateways (Alex) — target: EOD Thu 2028-03-16.
2) Redwood to provide a minimal acceptance checklist for POC (network ACLs, required private endpoints, expected firewall rules) — owner: Neha — will send by EOD today.
3) CedarCare security to review SOC2 excerpt and confirm KMS/HSM preferences (Priya) — target: Tue 2028-03-21.
4) Schedule a short infra runbook review with CedarCare infra (Alex + Ben) to validate NAT/firewall exceptions and a staged on-prem test (30–45 mins) — propose Tue 2028-03-21 10:00 PT.

Attachments: network-topology.png (requested diagram format), SOC2-excerpt.pdf (Redwood excerpt).

Open questions we need answered to scope POC
- Can you confirm whether prod nodes can accept inbound-only connections from a peering/VPN endpoint, i.e., no SNAT allowed?
- Do you have a preferred cert/key rotation cadence for HSM integration?
- Any procurement constraints that would prevent a 30–60 day POC in your environment?

If this aligns, I’ll circulate a short acceptance checklist + proposed test plan this afternoon and lock the runbook review for Tuesday.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0137

From: Samuel Trent <sam.trent@cedarcare.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@cedarcare.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cedarcare.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private/VPC qualification — connectivity & acceptance questions

Thanks Neha — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We cannot allow outbound internet from the prod VPC at all. Any egress must be via a managed peering (Azure ExpressRoute / AWS PrivateLink equivalent) or through our on-prem transit.
- For the POC, we can stand up a staging VPC with limited egress (approved jump host for updates) but the production-like environment must be fully isolated.
- Concurrency numbers look right; we’ll provide a sampled load profile.

Action: I’m adding Alex Mercer (infra) to this thread — Alex will send the network diagram and a technical owner for firewall rules. Expect the diagram by Thursday morning.

Also, our security team has asked for the following in addition to SOC2:
- A brief note on how Redwood handles KV cache persistence and whether any session state can be persisted off-host.
- A short e2e test plan showing how we can validate that there is zero outbound traffic during inference.

We’ll push back on procurement timing if we need additional legal review for an air-gapped on-prem SOW, but the POC door is open.

—Sam
Samuel Trent
Director of IT Operations | CedarCare Health
sam.trent@cedarcare.com | +1 (617) 555-2210
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Trent <sam.trent@cedarcare.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cedarcare.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private/VPC qualification — connectivity & acceptance questions

Appreciate the clarity, Sam. A couple of practical items from ops + a proposed minimal acceptance checklist (POC):

Minimal POC acceptance checklist (proposed)
- Private connectivity: peering/VPN established between CedarCare staging VPC and Redwood private endpoint; no SNAT from prod nodes.
- Authentication: mTLS for service-to-service traffic; Redwood to present cert chain — details in attached SOC2 excerpt.
- Keys: integration with your KMS/HSM for at-rest keys; Redwood supports bring-your-own-key workflows.
- Logging: audit logs forwarded to customer logging endpoint (syslog/S3) with 1-year retention; we will supply sample log format.
- Traffic validation: run a 10-minute blocked egress test during the POC to confirm no outbound connections.

Ben’s asks for CedarCare infra before the runbook review
- Shared network diagram (we need precise CIDR ranges and any NAT/PAT rules).
- Contact for VPN/peering requests (Alex).
- Preliminary procurement signal — is the POC covered under evaluation budget or do we need a formal PO?

I’ll attach the SOC2 excerpt and a short e2e test plan in a follow-up e-mail. If Alex can confirm availability, let’s lock Tue 03/21 10:00 PT for the runbook review.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0099

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cedarcare.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private/VPC qualification — connectivity & acceptance questions

Thanks all — forwarding our initial diagram as promised (attached link in separate e-mail). Quick replies inline: 

> Can you confirm whether prod nodes can accept inbound-only connections from a peering/VPN endpoint, i.e., no SNAT allowed?
Yes. Prod hosts will only accept inbound traffic from our transit via peering. No SNAT/PAT from prod allowed.

> Preferred cert/key rotation cadence for HSM integration?
We currently rotate TLS certs every 90 days and HSM keys yearly; open to align with Redwood for the POC.

> Procurement constraints for 30–60 day POC?
We can cover a short POC under our evaluation budget; longer on-prem engagements will need SOW and legal review.

I’ll send the network diagram and firewall rule set by Thu morning. Looking forward to the runbook review.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Infrastructure Lead | CedarCare Health
